title: Resume a VCF Automation deployment after access-token expiry
prompt:
Complete `vcf_automation/client.py` as a standard-library-only Python 3.11+ client for VCF Automation in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation, and it has no published specification in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. This focused contract was therefore derived from the authoritative Broadcom xAPIs 9.0 reference pages recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`; it is reference-documentation-derived, not specification-derived.

Preserve the public imports in `vcf_automation/__init__.py` and the declarations and signatures in `vcf_automation/client.py`. Implement `VcfAutomationClient(base_url, refresh_token, *, timeout=5.0)` and `request_catalog_item(catalog_item_id, request) -> DeploymentResult`. The method must exchange the supplied refresh token for a bearer access token, request one catalog item deployment, and poll that same deployment until its create status is terminal. Use only the three operations named in the contract and contact no other route.

The access token expires after the catalog request has created the deployment. When a deployment poll returns HTTP 401, obtain a new access token through `retrieveAuthToken`, then continue polling the existing deployment ID. Do not submit `requestCatalogItemInstances_1` again, and do not discard or replace the deployment ID returned by that successful request.

Send `Accept: application/json` on every request. JSON POSTs also send `Content-Type: application/json`; GETs are bodyless and do not send `Content-Type`. For authorized operations send exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` header. `retrieveAuthToken` has no bearer access token and sends no `Authorization` header. Paths substitute each identifier as one percent-encoded path segment. Omit all optional query parameters.

Encode both JSON bodies as compact UTF-8. The login body is the contract's `refreshToken` object. Build the catalog body in contract declaration order: `bulkRequestCount` when set, then `deploymentName`, `inputs`, `projectId`, `reason` when set, and `version` when set. A Python value of `None` means an optional field is unset and must be omitted completely; do not serialize it as `null`, an empty string, an empty object, zero, or a made-up default. Explicit non-`None` values must be preserved.

Require the documented HTTP statuses and response shapes. A successful catalog request must yield exactly one object with nonblank `deploymentId` and `deploymentName` strings. Poll while status is `CREATE_INPROGRESS`, return `DeploymentResult` only for `CREATE_SUCCESSFUL`, raise `DeploymentFailed` for `CREATE_FAILED`, and raise the provided contract/error types for other HTTP or malformed-response failures. Populate a successful result with the catalog response's deployment ID and the terminal deployment's `name`, optional `projectId` (or `None` when absent), and status.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts the supplied contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads its thread-safe in-memory request log. The mock derives its complete method/path allow-list from `docs/contract.json` and serves only the three named operations. Verification asserts the token refresh and continuation behavior, exact ordered raw targets, header values and multiplicity, byte-exact compact JSON, bodyless GETs, omission of every unset optional field and query parameter, absence of a duplicate deployment request, no extra calls, and standard-library-only imports. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `pyproject.toml` and `vcf_automation/__init__.py`, is protected. Edit only `vcf_automation/client.py`. Do not add dependencies or require package installation.
scenario: an access token expires after a catalog deployment is created and polling must continue on the same deployment after refreshing it
constraint: the loopback request log proves exact VCF Automation 9.0 wire shape and omission of unset optional fields
